blocks.text: sitting with Rasulullaah ﷺ when he looked towards the sky. An angel suddenly descended to which Hadhrat Jibra'eel (AS) said, "Since he has been created, this angel has never descended until this moment." When the angel came down, he said, "O Muhammad ﷺ! Your Rabb has sent me to you. (Allaah asks whether) 'Is it a Nabi who is a king that I should make you or a Rasool that is a slave (of Allaah)?'" Advising Rasulullaah ﷺ, Hadhrat Jibra'eel (AS) said, "Adopt humility before your Rabb, O Muhammad ﷺ!" Rasulullaah ﷺ then replied, "I would rather be a Rasool who is a slave."[^1]
Another narration from Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) adds at the end, "After this, Rasulullaah ﷺ never ate in a reclining position and would say, 'I eat as a slave eats and sit as a slave sits."
A similar narration[^2] from Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) has already passed.
A Narration of Hadhrat Abu Umaamah Baahili (RA)

Hadhrat Abu Ghaalib says that he once asked Hadhrat Abu Umaamah (RA) to narrate to them a Hadith that he had heard from Rasulullaah ﷺ. Hadhrat Abu Umaamah (RA) replied, "Everything that Rasulullaah ﷺ said was (according to) the Qur'aan. He made Dhikr in abundance, kept his lectures brief, lengthened his salaah and was never too stuck up, or proud to go with a poor or unimportant person to personally see to his needs."[^3]

Hadhrat Anas (RA) says, "Rasulullaah ﷺ made Dhikr in abundance, never engaged in futilities, rode a camel, wore woollen clothing and even accepted the invitations of slaves. If only you saw him (you would realise the extent of his humility) on the day the Battle of Khaybar was fought, he rode a donkey with reins made from the bark of a date palm."[^4] Another narration[^5] adds that Rasulullaah ﷺ also visited the ill and attended funerals.
The Narrations of Hadhrat Abu Moosa Ash'ari (RA), Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) and Hadhrat Anas (RA) in this Regard
Hadhrat Abu Moosa Ash'ari (RA) says, "Rasulullaah ﷺ used to ride a donkey, wear woollen clothes, hold down a goat and milk it and personally serve guests."[^6]
Ahmad, Bazzaar and Abu Ya'la, reporting from reliable sources as confirmed by Haythami (Vol.9 Pg.19).
